problems.title: Cosmological constant problem
problems.moniker: the worst prediction in physics (~120 orders of magnitude)
problems.statement: The magnitude of Λ is derived, not tuned: Λ·ℓ_P² = 13⁻¹⁰⁸/12 = 3/R² with R = 6·13⁵⁴ from Gaussian-lattice cell counting (0.1% in the exponent, 0.48% on R). The 120-order "catastrophe" is an artifact of computing vacuum energy in a framework where Λ is an input; here it is a counting output.
problems.test: Tighter joint (Λ, H₀) determinations move R; the identity fails if the exponent drifts beyond its 0.1% window.

problems.title: Dark energy fraction / cosmic coincidence problem
problems.moniker: why is Ω_Λ order unity now?
problems.statement: The bare Farey partition 13:5:1 over 19 supplies a substrate-side reference point Ω_Λ = 13/19 ≈ 0.684 — canonical per D1/C16 as a reference, not a prediction (the same partition puts Ω_b = 1/19, 6.7% from observation). The two-component refinement (w₊ = 13/14, Ω_Λ = 181/264) is retracted to Class 2: w₊ is a numerical fit to Planck values and is computed by no script in the repo. The coincidence problem is open here; the partition is bookkeeping until a derivation forces the weights.

problems.title: Dark matter and baryon fractions
problems.statement: The bare partition gives Ω_DM : Ω_b = 5 : 1 against an observed ≈ 5.4 — a reference ratio, not a prediction (D1/C16). The two-component numbers previously quoted here (Ω_DM = 35/132, Ω_b = 13/264, ratio 70/13) inherit Class 2 from the fitted w₊ = 13/14 closure and are computed by no script. What fixes the ratio is open, at the fraction level and the particle level alike.
problems.caveats: No particle candidate is offered; galactic phenomenology is handled by the a₀ row below and does not depend on this partition.

problems.title: Strong CP problem
problems.statement: θ_QCD = 0 via Pin⁺(3) topology (D45) — conditional, retracted from Class 5 (2026-08-12): the derivation runs entirely on the K² configuration space, whose selection is an unsettled premise, and the eta-invariant input is an unverified import. If those premises hold, the substrate admits no θ-term: no axion, no tuning.
problems.test: Any measurement of θ ≠ 0 falsifies the conditional chain outright; discovery of a QCD axion doing the resolving would undercut the mechanism.

problems.title: Quantum measurement problem
problems.moniker: often called the most embarrassing problem in physics
problems.statement: Dissolved, not solved-by-interpretation: the substrate carries no projection postulate to reconcile with unitary evolution. Collapse is fidelity-bounded self-measurement; the preferred basis is basin selection (the saddle-node normal form fixes each context's basis structurally); the Born exponent 2 is saddle-node universality, not an axiom.
problems.test: Collapse duration τ ∝ 1/√ε with τΔω = const, and Zeno suppression, from the fidelity bound — testable in cavity QED / superconducting qubits.
problems.caveats: The dissolution docs are Class-3 articulations resting on the Class-5 Born-rule apparatus; the falsifiable content lives in the collapse-timing predictions.

problems.title: Bell nonlocality / EPR
problems.moniker: how can correlations violate Bell bounds without signaling?
problems.statement: Bell-violating, non-signaling statistics at exactly the Tsirelson bound (and Mermin |M| = 4 for GHZ) are derived substrate-internally. Bell's no-go is evaded honestly: the conserved Q mod 2 is a global topological invariant of the Klein-bottle context window, not a shared local hidden variable λ.
problems.caveats: Reproduces QM's bounds rather than predicting deviations from them; the claim is structural explanation, not new statistics.

problems.title: Dimensionality and signature of spacetime
problems.statement: Open (demoted from the scorecard 2026-08-06, D2 disposition). d = 3 was claimed via the identification M = SL(2,ℝ), but the continuum-completion step names no mathematical operation (SL(2,ℤ) is discrete and closed in SL(2,ℝ)), and the same premises admit d = 2 and d = 1. The signature argument rests on a sign rule that contradicts the orientation character being a homomorphism. SL(2,ℂ) = Spin(3,1) is a true imported theorem; every arrow leading to it is open.

problems.title: Origin of the Standard Model gauge group
problems.moniker: why SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1), why do anomalies cancel?
problems.statement: SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) is read off the Klein-bottle mode lattice Z₆ = Z₂ × Z₃ (D41/D42) — conditional, retracted from Class 5 (2026-08-12): the 12-transition count consumes the 4-mode roster, which rests on the conjectured XOR parity translation (xor_derivation §5). The 6 SM anomaly conditions are verified for the imported charge assignment (D41 hardcodes the hypercharges); Gell-Mann–Nishijima holds with Y back-solved, not derived. Yang-Mills uniqueness via Utiyama + Cartan is the strongest leg, conditional on the same kinematics.

problems.title: Unification of general relativity and quantum mechanics
problems.statement: GR and QM are the two continuum limits of one substrate: Einstein's equations unique (Lovelock, D13) at the locked K=1 limit, Schrödinger structure at K<1, with the K=1 ↔ K<1 decoupling non-smooth — which is why the two theories resist merger in the continuum and why each needs its own anchor.
problems.caveats: Unification is at the substrate layer; no quantum-gravity phenomenology (e.g. graviton scattering) is predicted.

problems.statement: a₀ = cH₀/(2π) structurally from Λ (both scales are set by Λ, so the coincidence is an identity), and the RAR interpolating shape with its scatter pattern derived from the fidelity bound rather than fit.
problems.test: a₀(z) = cH(z)/(2π) at high z (GEKO/CRISTAL ~2025–2030): z≈5 galaxies Newtonian at z=0 should sit in the transition zone; post-merger RAR re-establishment on ~1/H(z).

Two dimensional anchors (H₀, v_EW) are proven structurally minimal (prime-5 obstruction: the canonical register's prime support {2,3} cannot reach 15 for the 13⁻¹⁵ target); the near-match v/M_P ≈ 13⁻¹⁵ (3.1%) is Class-2 numerology, declined with executed nulls.

The nulls are documented but not reproducible from this tree.
